purpose: Additional comparative glossary, textual witnesses and separately attributed critical apparatus. Adopted readings are explicitly linked to changes in the reading text; later philosophical commentary remains separate from the authorial text.

glossary.definition: The intellect in actuality as possessing intelligible contents, distinguished from initial receptivity or mere potentiality.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Dependence of a cause upon its own effect through a reciprocal causal sequence, not merely reciprocal logical implication.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Quiddity considered excluding an accompanying determination; central to certain discussions of genus, differentia, and form.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Quiddity considered together with a positive determination, such as humanity with the features of an individual.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The opposition of a proposition and its negation under the same respect, without an intermediate truth value in the classical account.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Opposition between contrary positive characteristics within one field; unlike contradiction, contraries may admit an intermediate.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The substantial form by which a material composite has three-dimensional extension in the author's analysis.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Opposition between correlative terms such as parent/child or above/below, where the meaning of each includes reference to the other.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Specification or determination of an existent. In discussions of existence, determination by degree must be distinguished from determination by a quiddity.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The essential determination distinguishing a species within a genus; distinguish this from a proprium that merely accompanies it.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The determination of one item as other than another; what grounds the distinction depends on whether the discussion concerns concepts, quiddities, or concrete existents.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: That which brings an effect into existence, with distinctions between complete and incomplete or preparatory forms of agency.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A context-sensitive term for a thing's being established or obtaining. It must not automatically be identified with external existence in debates about non-existent things.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An existent whose being, while actualising its own nature, also removes a privation from another, such as an accidental quality informing a subject.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Existence that actualises its own essence without thereby constituting the accidental perfection of a different subject; not identical to necessary existence.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Existence outside the mind, where a thing's characteristic external effects obtain, contrasted with the existence of its intelligible form in cognition.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The end for whose sake an operation is undertaken or made intelligible; not restricted to conscious intention in the author's account.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The first separate intellectual effect in the emanative hierarchy of the author's philosophical account; not to be identified uncritically with the Necessary Existent.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The determining substantial principle through which a material thing is the kind of thing that it is.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An essential universal shared by different species. A genus alone does not constitute a full essential definition.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An ontological level of imaginal forms described as distinct both from gross matter and from purely intellectual existence.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Existence intelligible as a subject of predication on its own, in contrast to a linking existence; independence of signification is not unrestricted causal independence.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The actuality whereby something is this individual rather than another. Tabāṭabāʾī connects individuation ultimately with existence, not a mere aggregation of universal predicates.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An unending sequence; its impossibility in the relevant demonstration concerns an existentially ordered chain of causes, not every infinite series.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: What is grasped by intellect under an intelligible form; in intellectual self-presence, knower and intelligible are discussed as united.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A quiddity, considered in itself, does not require either its existence or its non-existence; this is not the same as physical dispositional potential.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The receptive material principle of a composite substance; not identical with the agent that imparts actuality.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The nature considered as a common essence without the mind's extra consideration of its universality as a logical predicate.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Existence considered necessary rather than merely possible. The author sharply distinguishes necessity through another from intrinsic necessity.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Necessity following upon a sufficient cause, as distinct from necessary existence through the thing's own reality.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A real capacity for an actuality, especially in the analysis of temporal coming-to-be; distinguish from merely conceivable possibility.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The position opposed to the primacy of existence: quiddity, rather than existence, is taken as fundamental in external reality. It must not be confused with the trivial claim that things have quiddities.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The purely potential, indeterminate principle in material substance, not a free-standing physical stuff with its own actuality.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An accidental category, including dispositions and qualities; not all uses of the ordinary word 'how' denote the technical category.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A category concerned with divisible magnitude or number, not to be confused with the relational category of place or position.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The accidental category ordered toward another. Distinguish it from the existential dependency that constitutes the effect as related to its cause.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Necessity considered in relation to another existent, particularly where correlatives imply one another, not a separate sufficient cause.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The absence of motion in a subject capable of moving, rather than absolute immutability without regard to motion.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The disputed possibility that numerically the same thing, after wholly ceasing to exist, could return. This is different from survival or transformation.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: An immaterial principle in its essence but connected with the body in its operation; its precise status differs from a wholly separate intellect.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A complete specific nature resulting from the appropriate essential determination of a genus.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Change in substantial existence itself, not merely in its quantity, quality, or spatial location; central to the Sadrāian framework.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: Existence considered as a reality, not merely the common concept signified by the word 'existence'. The distinction is indispensable for interpreting gradation.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The status of being a thing; the author argues that genuine thingness is coextensive with existence, rejecting a positive intermediate status for non-existents.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The measure of motion in the author's analysis, linked to the successive renewal and division of material existence.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: The unity ascribed to pure necessary existence: not numerical oneness that admits another member of the same order.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

glossary.definition: A way of considering quiddity without stipulating either the presence or the absence of a further determination; variants of this consideration must be distinguished.
glossary.editorialOrigin: Comparative terminology, prepared as an additional gloss from the Bidāya reader; not a statement by the author of Nihāya.

criticalNotes.type: Historical correction · later editor
criticalNotes.text: The 1428 AH editor's long note listing eight positions on the reality of existence (vol. 1, printed p. 34) groups ‘Tomas Akoims’ (Thomas Aquinas) with absolute equivocation between God and creatures. This attribution is inaccurate: Aquinas, Summa theologiae I, q. 13, a. 5, explicitly rejects both univocal and purely equivocal predication in favour of analogy. This correction concerns the later editor's note; it is not a criticism of an assertion in Tabatabai's authorial chapter. Primary reference: https://www.newadvent.org/summa/1013.htm.
criticalNotes.source: 1428 AH Zāriʿī ed., vol. 1 pp. 33–34; Aquinas ST I q13 a5

criticalNotes.type: Authorial footnote attribution
criticalNotes.text: In the corrected 1428 AH witness (vol. 1, printed p. 36) the short footnote on negating a limit is explicitly marked ‘منه رحمه الله’ (‘from the author’). It explains that, because limitation has the character of negation, denying limitation is a negation of negation and therefore affirms the pure actuality of existence. The attribution is authorial; the surrounding longer explanatory footnotes belong to the later editor.

This reconciliation is a later editorial gloss, not an authorial assertion to be inserted into Tabāṭabāʾī's matn; its reading of Ṭūsī requires separate verification against Kashf al-Murād.

criticalNotes.type: Textual emendation · later editor
criticalNotes.text: The 1417 base says «ينتزع من الموضوعين الواجدين للنسبة المتكرّرة المتلازمة وصفاً ناعتاً لهما». In vol. 1 p. 218 n. 4 the 1428 editor prints «ينتزع لكلّ من الموضوعين ... وصفاً ناعتاً له» and explicitly records the earlier copy reading. The correction changes the analysis from one common property attributed jointly to both relata to one relational predicate of each term, dependent on their reciprocal relation. Both Arabic and English were corrected; old wording remains in the authorial passage note. The nearby «لوقوعها» was already correct in the 1417 reader. In the same chapter (vol. 1 p. 218 n. 1) he also corrects «المضاف إلى الابن» to «المضاف إلى الأب», since the subject bearing sonship is related to a father. The reader adopts this correction in both Arabic and English and retains the prior wording as a documented copy reading.

criticalNotes.type: Textual emendation · 1428 AH editor; early reading preserved
criticalNotes.text: The complete IX.9 authorial chapter was compared with the 1404 Qum facsimile, printed pp.210–212 (NYU canvases 214–216), and the later 1428 edition, vol.2 pp.107–110. The early print at p.211 and the 1417 base at p.265 both read «كما في القسم الأول» (as in the first kind). The 1428 editor explicitly records this copy reading and corrects it to «كما في القسم الثاني» at vol.2 p.108 n.4. The reader adopts the attributed later correction: stripping off and putting on belongs to the second, parallel kind, whereas the first, hierarchical kind is putting on after putting on. The English now says “as in the second kind.” The early facsimile does NOT attest الثاني. This resolves the previously unadopted internal conjecture; the original note identifier is preserved for continuity. No manuscript attestation or specialist certification is claimed.

criticalNotes.type: Later printed editor's conceptual objection · boundary of continuum
criticalNotes.text: In the 1428 AH revised edition, vol. 1, printed p.185–186, editor al-Zāriʿī objects (p.186 n.2) to the author's illustration that an intermediate segment of a divided line can serve as the shared boundary between adjacent segments. The editor insists that a shared boundary is outside both adjacent magnitudinal parts: a point between two parts of a line, a line between parts of a surface, a surface between portions of a body, and an instant between portions of time. Otherwise a discrete number such as seven could be divided into three, one, three and the middle unit incorrectly counted as a common boundary, erasing the distinction between continuous and discrete quantity. The author's 1417 Arabic wording and its literal English remain unchanged; attach the editor's argument as criticism, not an attested manuscript emendation. The wording of the author's example is also present in the later digital print; no alternative original reading claimed.
criticalNotes.source: Nihāyat al-Ḥikma, ed. ʿAbbās ʿAlī al-Zāriʿī, 4th ed., Qum 1428 AH, vol. 1, printed p.186 n.2; authorial chapter IX on quantity in Stage VI (N-VI-09), base 1417 AH pp.139–141

criticalNotes.type: Intertextual authorial qualification · substance genus and substantial forms
criticalNotes.text: The 1428 revised editor at vol. 1, printed p.154 n.1 points to Muḥammad Taqī al-Āmulī's position and cross-refers to Ṭabāṭabāʾī's *Bidāyat al-Ḥikma* p.87, where the initial definition includes an elemental substantial form inhering in matter that depends upon that form. The *Nihāyat* chapter, however, insists that substantial forms are simple quiddities not species falling directly under the genus of substance. Compare the user's bilingual *Bidāya* units B-VI-01 and B-VI-02: B-VI-01 permits 'substance' as an existential descriptor of form in dependent matter; B-VI-02 expressly states that corporeal form enters the fivefold classification only incidentally, because a differentia taken *bi-sharṭ lā* does not fall under the genus of substance even if substance is predicated of it. Accordingly, do not call the two authorial works unqualifiedly contradictory or silently harmonize them: distinguish definitional description, genre membership, and common vs primary predication. This is an analytical reconciliation, not a newly discovered variant or final doctrinal adjudication.
criticalNotes.source: 1428 al-Zāriʿī edition, vol. 1 printed pp.153–155 n.1; compare *Bidāyat al-Ḥikma* local authorial units B-VI-01 and B-VI-02, Arabic reader source https://lib.rafed.net/m/?b_id=1571&type=c_fbook
criticalNotes.status: Later edition footnote cross-reference and exact two local Bidāya Arabic chapter checks; interpretive comparison, not print variant
criticalNotes.subject: substance vs form; genus vs common predication

criticalNotes.type: Grammatical recast · 1428 AH editor
criticalNotes.text: The early 1404 facsimile p.211 and the 1417 base p.265 read «هي الموضوع بعينه ما تعاقبت». The 1428 editor, vol.2 p.108 n.3, recasts this as «هي بعينها موضوع ما تعاقبت». The reader adopts that disclosed grammatical recast; the claim that the same matter persists through the succession of forms is unchanged. The later note quotes its copies with «تعاقب» without a final feminine ت, whereas the directly inspected early facsimile and the current 1417 transcription have «تعاقبت». The collective copy report must not be substituted for the exact reading of either inspected witness. The English already conveys the same subject claim.
criticalNotes.status: Explicit later editorial recast; not manuscript-attested

criticalNotes.type: Pronoun correction · 1428 AH editor
criticalNotes.text: The 1404 early print p.212 and the 1417 base p.266 have the masculine possessive in «قوة لقوته» (base with vocalization: «قوّةً لقوّته»). The 1428 editor, vol.2 p.109 n.2, corrects the pronoun to the feminine «لقوّتها», referring to «فعليّة ما». The reading text adopts «قوّةً لقوّتها». The English already refers to an actuality’s own potentiality and is unchanged. This pronoun correction is separate from the editor’s philosophical objection to the argument against descending motion.

Adopted: يرجعان إلى بطلان الوجوب الذاتيّ → يرجعان إلى نفي بطلان الوجوب الذاتيّ. Here the subjects are the impossibility of quiddity and the impossibility of possibility, so they amount to denying the nullification of intrinsic necessity. Earlier A18 instead concerns the impossible attributes themselves and correctly reduces them to denial of necessity. Preserves that crucial change of negative scope. Grade: explicit-later-editor-emendation; earlier-reading-retained-in-apparatus. Source: 1404 pp. 68; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 115 n. 2

Adopted: فامتناع الماهيّة التي سلكنا إلى بيانه → فامتناع الماهيّة الذي سلكنا إلى بيانه. The masculine relative agrees with امتناع, the object explained and antecedent of بيانه; the early feminine follows the nearer الماهية. Meaning already represented in English. Grade: unfootnoted-later-edition-reading; contextual-grammatical-justification. Source: 1404 pp. 68; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 115

Adopted: وعرْضُها في الذهن → وعروضُها في الذهن. The early scan clearly preserves عروض, the technical accruing/predication term paired with external اتصاف. The direct Bidāya parallel B-IV-09 likewise reads عروضها. Later digital عرضها lacks the internal wāw; record this disagreement explicitly. Existing English presentation as predicates already conveys the intended conceptual relation. Grade: early-facsimile-reading-against-later-digital; not-a-later-editor-emendation. Source: 1404 pp. 69; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 116

Adopted: For example, the impossibility of a quiddity, which we establish by way of the impossibility of possibility for Him, exalted is He, and the impossibility of possibility itself both ultimately amount to the nullification of intrinsic necessity, which is impossible for Him. The intellect has brought this nullification before itself in conjunction with the intrinsic necessity abstracted from the very essence. → For example, the impossibility of a quiddity, which we establish by way of the impossibility of possibility for Him, exalted is He, and the impossibility of possibility itself both ultimately amount to denying the nullification of intrinsic necessity, a nullification that is impossible for Him. The intellect has brought this denial before itself in conjunction with the intrinsic necessity abstracted from the very essence.. Conditional on adopting the explicit p.115 n.2 insertion نفي; n.3 confirms that the final pronoun refers to this denial. Distinguishes denying necessity from denying its nullification. Grade: source-linked-English-revision. Source: 1404 pp. 65,66,67,68,69,70; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 111,112,113,114,115,116

Adopted: والمعلول الواحد لا تكون لها إلاّ علّةً واحدةً → والمعلول الواحد لا تكون له إلاّ علّةٌ واحدةٌ. The masculine pronoun refers grammatically to المعلول; later p.174 attests له without a dedicated variant note. Fresh inspection shows that early p.103 actually reads لها, contradicting report C. Retain the early/base feminine verb تكون because its postposed subject is علّة, and make that subject and its adjective nominative. This is a mixed later-reading and contextual-vocalization decision, not mere orthography. Grade: unfootnoted-later-consonantal-reading-plus-contextual-vocalization; corrected-early-attestation. Source: 1404 pp. 103; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 174

Adopted: الفصل السادس — في أنّ المادّة لا تفارق الجسميّة والجسميّة لا تفارق — المادّة أي أنّ كلّ واحدة منهما لا تفارق صاحبتها → الفصل السادس — في أنّ المادّة لا تفارق الجسميّة والجسميّة لا تفارق المادّة، أي أنّ كلّ واحدة منهما لا تفارق صاحبتها. Remove the spurious em dash between تفارق and its object المادة; retain both complete source heading clauses and the subtitle. The منها/منهما witness difference is recorded separately in originalHeadings. Grade: reader-heading-punctuation; authorial-clauses-preserved. Source: 1404 pp. 103; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 173

criticalNotes.type: External comparison · new Stage X review
criticalNotes.text:
Qum 1404 printed pp. 288–292 (canvases 292–296); 1428 edited digital text, vol. 2 pp. 245–251. Stage X compared every stored Arabic and English paragraph with the complete early printed chapter and the later digital chapter, including the chapter boundaries and all associated later editorial notes. The early witness is a facsimile; the 1428 witness is a digital presentation, not a facsimile. No manuscript or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

Adopted [N1]: «العلم بعدالإيجاد» → «العلم بعد الإيجاد». Separate بعد from الإيجاد without changing the reading. Evidence: 1404 pp. 289–290 / canvases 293–294; 1428 p. 248.

Adopted [N1]: «مرتبة وجوداتهاالممكنة» → «مرتبة وجوداتها الممكنة». Separate the noun and its adjective without altering the argument. Evidence: 1404 pp. 289–290 / canvases 293–294; 1428 p. 248.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «العلم بالمسموعات والعلم بالمبصرات من مطلق العلم»; later proposal «العلم بالمسموعات والعلم بالمبصرات ، فهما من مطلق العلم». The later unfootnoted فهما supplies an explicit syntactic resumption. The earlier wording is intelligible and is retained; the English already conveys the predication. Evidence: 1404 p. 289 / canvas 293; 1428 p. 246.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «لبيان تحقُّق العلم»; later proposal «لبيان نحو تحقُّق العلم». The later editor adds نحو and appeals to Bidaya. The following clause already specifies union; no need to introduce a word absent from the early print. Evidence: 1404 p. 290 / canvas 294; 1428 p. 248 n. 4.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «لا بالعروض ونحوه»; later proposal «لا بالعرض ونحوه». Retain the coherent earlier expression for inherence; the later lexical preference is attributed. Evidence: 1404 p. 290 / canvas 294; 1428 p. 248 n. 5.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «فله (تعالى) علمٌ إجماليّ بها بتبع علمه بذاته.»; later proposal «[وأمّا قبل الإيحاد] فله (تعالى) علمٌ إجماليّ بها بتبع علمه بذاته.». The editor explicitly says the bracketed supplement is absent from the copies. Its digital text also prints الإيحاد. Neither the supplement nor an unmarked correction of its typo enters the authorial body. Evidence: 1404 p. 290 / canvas 294; 1428 p. 249 n. 1.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «إنّ ذاته المتعالية علْمٌ تفصيليٌّ بالمعلول الأوّل»; later proposal «إنّ لذاته المتعالية علْمٌ تفصيليٌّ بالمعلول الأوّل». The editor calls the possessive construction preferable. It changes identity into possession in a reported position; preserve the earlier identity formulation and matching English. Evidence: 1404 p. 291 / canvas 295; 1428 p. 250 n. 3.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «وذات المعلول الأوّل علْمٌ تفصيليٌّ بالمعلول الثاني»; later proposal «ولذات المعلول الأوّل علْمٌ تفصيليٌّ بالمعلول الثاني». Preserve the second identity formulation for the same reason; this is not a typographical correction. Evidence: 1404 p. 291 / canvas 295; 1428 p. 250 n. 4.

English comparison: Every stored English paragraph was compared with its Arabic and both external witnesses. The distinctions between knowledge before/after creation, detailed/comprehensive knowledge, and acquired/presential knowledge are preserved. The existing note defining comprehensive (ijmali) as undivided rather than incomplete knowledge is retained. No English body correction is justified in this pass.

Later editorial commentary, separate from the authorial argument:

1428 vol. 2 245 nn. 1–4 — Cross-references and proof analysis: References to XI.1/XI.11 and IV.4/XII.4, the unpacking into two syllogisms of the self-knowledge proof, and the referent of the existential perfections were read. The expanded syllogisms are the later editor’s exposition.

1428 vol. 2 246 n. 1 and n. 2 continued through 247 — Causal references and hearing/seeing debate: The editor cites VIII.5 and XII.9, then quotes Sadra, Asfar 6:422, on hearing and seeing as specific presential cognitions distinct from unqualified knowledge. He next quotes Tabatabai’s separate Asfar annotation rejecting that restriction because all categories are present to God and divine knowledge is wholly presential. The latter is an attributed quotation from another work, not an original footnote of this Nihaya chapter.

1428 vol. 2 247 nn. 1–3 — Reported historical attributions and vocabulary: The editor distinguishes denial of divine knowledge from denial of knowledge of others, quotes Tusi on the transmission of these positions, glosses mahjuj as defeated, and cites Shahrastani for Hisham b. Amr al-Fuwati and Abu Bakr al-Asamm. These historical attributions are reported as editorial claims, not independently established here.

1428 vol. 2 248 nn. 1–7 — References, proposed emendations, and school attributions: All references for Plato and Porphyry, the two explicit alterations نحو and بالعرض, the report of Suhrawardi’s spiritual encounter with Aristotle, and the named later followers Tusi, Shirazi, Ibn Kammuna and Shahrazuri were read. The altered words are registered separately and the historical narrative remains attributed.

1428 vol. 2 249 nn. 1–4 — Supplement, disagreement, and Milesian identification: The bracketed before-creation supplement is expressly absent from the copies. The editor quotes Sabzawari’s Asfar 6:165 annotation against the author: material things are absent to us but present to an encompassing divine knower. This disagreement is not blended into the author’s reply. The editor identifies al-Malati as Thales and contrasts an account attributed to Anaximenes, with cited secondary transmission.

1428 vol. 2 250 nn. 1–6 — Qualification of a cross-reference and later preferences: The editor says the claimed earlier proof is not explicit in this book and points instead to VI.15/XI.11; identifies the sixth account with some philosophers and Sabzawari; prefers لذاته and ولذات in notes 3–4; and supplies sources for later thinkers and the Peripatetic account. The identity-to-possession alteration is not adopted.

1428 vol. 2 251 nn. 1–4 — Logical and school references: References for the logical universal, Muʿtazilite fixity of nonexistents, I.2, and the Sufi positions linked to Ibn Arabi and Qunawi were read. The cited earlier works themselves were not independently collated.

criticalNotes.text:
Qum 1404 printed pp. 292–296 (canvases 296–300); 1428 edited digital text, vol. 2 pp. 252–257. Stage X compared every stored Arabic and English paragraph with the complete early printed chapter and the later digital chapter, including the chapter boundaries and all associated later editorial notes. The early witness is a facsimile; the 1428 witness is a digital presentation, not a facsimile. No manuscript or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

Layout correction: remove the stray transcription separator between the judicial example and its analysis; no authorial text is removed.

Adopted [N1]: «بماله من الخصوصيّات» → «بما له من الخصوصيّات». Normalize the word boundary while deliberately retaining the early masculine pronoun, which can refer to existence. Evidence: 1404 p. 293 / canvas 297; 1428 p. 253 n. 1.

Adopted [N2]: «والبناء يقدّر ما يريده من البنّاء» → «والبنّاء يقدّر ما يريده من البناء». Correct the reversed builder/building vocalization. The consonantal text is unchanged, the later vocalization and context distinguish the agent from the building, and the existing English is already correct. Evidence: 1404 p. 294 / canvas 298; 1428 p. 255.

Adopted [N2]: «الصور العلمّيّة» → «الصور العلميّة». Move the misplaced shadda from mim to ya in the adjective علمیّة; this is a limited vocalization repair, not an exhaustive diplomatic normalization. Evidence: 1404 p. 295 / canvas 299; 1428 p. 255.

Adopted [N1]: «يحدّبها فعل الإنسان» → «يحدّ بها فعل الإنسان». Separate the verb from the attached next word; preserve the wording and existing English. Evidence: 1404 p. 295 / canvas 299; 1428 p. 256.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «بماله من الخصوصيّات المعلومة»; later proposal «بما لها من الخصوصيّات المعلومة». The later editor prefers a feminine reference to things. The earlier masculine can refer to their existence. Only word spacing is normalized by AR02; the pronoun is retained. Evidence: 1404 p. 293 / canvas 297; 1428 p. 253 n. 1.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «نسبتها إلى عللها التامّة»; later proposal «نسبتها إلى علّتها التامّة». The distributive plural of complete causes is coherent for plural contingent existents. Retain it rather than impose the later singular. Evidence: 1404 p. 293 / canvas 297; 1428 p. 253 n. 2.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «الكثيف من الأجسام ذا اللون»; later proposal «الكثيف من الأجسام ذي اللون». The accusative ذا may qualify الكثيف as the object of seeing. The later genitive is an explicit editorial preference, not compelled by the earlier syntax. Evidence: 1404 p. 295 / canvas 299; 1428 p. 255 n. 2.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «حدودٌ ألحقها بها العللُ الناقصة»; later proposal «حدودٌ ألحقتها بها العللُ الناقصة». The postponed nonhuman broken-plural subject permits the earlier masculine verb. Retain the earlier form while recording the later agreement choice. Evidence: 1404 p. 295 / canvas 299; 1428 p. 255 n. 3.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «حتّى يعمّم الماهيّات الإمكانيّة»; later proposal «حتّى يعمّ الماهيّات الإمكانيّة». Early print really reads يعمم, agreeing with the base. The later unfootnoted يعمّ is smoother for encompasses, but cannot be presented as a reading agreed by both witnesses. Preserve the early form and disclose the contextual English rendering. Evidence: 1404 p. 295 / canvas 299, checked again with magnification; 1428 p. 256.

Unresolved compression: both early p. 294 and later p. 255 say that the builder constructs according to what he determined, followed by لأسباب متجدّدة توجب عليه ذلك. Neither consulted witness supplies an intervening change-of-plan clause. The current English retains the transmitted sequence; no conjectural clause is added. The early printed Asfar 6:292 reference following the quotation is restored as a separate source note.

English comparison: All stored English was compared with the full Arabic and witnesses, including the complete Asfar quotation, both craft analogies, the conditions of vision, the choice objection and the extension to quiddities. The builder passage remains awkward in both witnesses; the English follows that text without inventing a missing revision of the plan. The reading encompasses for يعمّم is a contextual rendering; the later witness’s يعمّ is recorded, not silently back-projected. No English body change is adopted.

Later editorial commentary, separate from the authorial argument:

1428 vol. 2 252 n. 1 — General sources: References to Isharat, Asfar and Manzuma on the divisions of divine knowledge were read as references, not as independently collated witnesses.

1428 vol. 2 252 n. 2 — Different schemes of divine knowledge: The editor reports Sadra’s five degrees—providence, pen, tablet, decree and measure—and Sabzawari’s additional register of being. This taxonomy is later commentary.

1428 vol. 2 252 n. 3 continued through 253 — Survey of providence and separate authorial gloss: The full discussion of views on providence and definitions associated with Suhrawardi, Avicenna, Sadra, Sabzawari and Qunawi was read. It includes an attributed quotation of Tabatabai’s separate Asfar 6:291 gloss deriving providence from the goal and the divine essence. That quotation is not an original note of this Nihaya chapter.

1428 vol. 2 253 nn. 1–3 — Pronoun/number preferences and causal objection: The later editor prefers بما لها to بماله and علّتها التامة to عللها التامة. The earlier readings admit, respectively, reference to existence and distributive plural causes. The editor’s stronger claim about God alone being truly a cause is kept distinct from the author’s series of subordinate causes.

1428 vol. 2 254 nn. 1–5 — Source citation and referents: The cited source of the prevalent decree account, the Asfar 6:291–292 quotation reference, two Sadra referent glosses and the two accounts under discussion were read.

1428 vol. 2 255 nn. 1–3 — Lexical gloss and grammatical preferences: Qaʿa is glossed as a courtyard or tract of land. The editor explicitly changes ذا اللون to ذي اللون and ألحقها to ألحقتها. The earlier accusative can qualify the object of seeing, and the delayed nonhuman plural subject permits the earlier masculine verb; both earlier readings are retained.

1428 vol. 2 256 nn. 1–5 — Internal cross-references: All references for limits, freedom of choice, contingency and negative composition were read: XII.4, IV.5, VIII.3, IV.1 and XII.4.

1428 vol. 2 257 n. 1, complete — Comparative decree/measure discussion: The full note compares Damad’s Qabasat 418 account of the world as whole/articulated and Sabzawari’s universal intellect versus planetary soul forms. It then presents three differences inferred from the author and his Asfar 6:292 gloss: decree through complete cause versus measure through partial causes; measure concerning material things versus decree also including immaterial things; and unchanging decree versus measure that can change or fail. These are the later editor’s comparative claims, not additions to the authorial conclusion.

criticalNotes.text:
Qum 1404 printed pp. 296–300 (canvases 300–304); 1428 edited digital text, vol. 2 pp. 258–264. Stage X compared every stored Arabic and English paragraph with the complete early printed chapter and the later digital chapter, including the chapter boundaries and all associated later editorial notes. The early witness is a facsimile; the 1428 witness is a digital presentation, not a facsimile. No manuscript or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

Adopted [E1]: «الفواعل الطبيعيّة العادمة للشهور» → «الفواعل الطبيعيّة العادمة للشعور». The early print clearly has الشعور, awareness. The base and later digital witness share الشهور, months. The source and context justify the correction; the existing English already says awareness. Evidence: 1404 p. 297 / canvas 301; compare 1428 p. 258, which still prints للشهور.

Adopted [N2]: «القدرة المجردّة عن النواقص» → «القدرة المجرّدة عن النواقص». Correct the misplaced shadda to the form المجرّدة. Consonants and philosophical content are unchanged. Evidence: 1404 p. 298 / canvas 302; 1428 p. 259.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «فالخير محبوبٌ مطلقاً»; later proposal «فالخير محبوبٌ له مطلقاً». The later digital text adds له without an editorial note. The early text and base omit it; the context supplies the agent and no addition is needed. Evidence: 1404 p. 297 / canvas 301; 1428 p. 259.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «لا سبيل لتطرّق الشوق عليه»; later proposal «لا سبيل لتطرّق الشوق إليه». The early print agrees with عليه. Record the later unfootnoted prepositional alteration without treating it as a correction proved by both witnesses. Evidence: 1404 p. 297 / canvas 301; 1428 p. 259.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «بإرادة ومشيّة»; later proposal «بإرادة ومشيئة». Record the later editor’s explicit standardized spelling; do not relabel it as the early reading. The meaning and English volition are unchanged. Evidence: 1404 pp. 298–299 / canvases 302–303; 1428 p. 262 n. 1.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «وجود الإرادة والمشيّة»; later proposal «وجود الإرادة والمشيئة». The second explicit spelling normalization has the same status; preserve the earlier orthography in this pass. Evidence: 1404 p. 299 / canvas 303; 1428 p. 262 n. 2.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «فما بالها تنتزع»; later proposal «فما بالها أن تنتزع». The earlier ما بالها followed by a verbal clause is intelligible. The editor’s added أن is not necessary to recover the argument. Evidence: 1404 p. 299 / canvas 303; 1428 p. 263 n. 5.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «استحال أن يتّصف به الذات الواجبة بالذات»; later proposal «استحال أن تتّصف بها الذات الواجبة بالذات». The later agreement correction makes the antecedent action attributes explicit. Preserve the early reading pending further textual evidence and disclose that English them interprets the referent as those attributes; do not claim the earlier grammar is unproblematic. Evidence: 1404 p. 300 / canvas 304; 1428 p. 263 n. 6.

Recorded variant; earlier body retained: «بنحو العروض»; later proposal «بنحو العرض». Retain the earlier inherence/occurrence wording consistently with the other such loci; record the later explicit lexical preference. Evidence: 1404 p. 300 / canvas 304; 1428 p. 264 n. 1.

English comparison: Every English paragraph was checked against the complete Arabic and both witnesses. Awareness already translates the intended الشعور and needs no change. The distinction between human will as a psychic quality, the unproved identification of divine essential knowledge with will, and will abstracted from the station of act is preserved. The English plural them interprets the earlier awkward به in reference to the action attributes; that interpretation and the later editor’s بها are disclosed. No English body correction is adopted.

Later editorial commentary, separate from the authorial argument:

1428 vol. 2 258 n. 1 — Choice gloss: The editor explains self-determination as what the agent’s own essence requires. This is an explanatory gloss.

1428 vol. 2 259 nn. 1–6 — Syntax, references and ontological explanation: All six notes were read: the attachment of من القيود, the reference to XII.6, power as an existential perfection, the reasoning from psychic quality through accident/quiddity/limitation to lack, the ellipsis excluding will, and the referent of إذا كان.

1428 vol. 2 260 n. 1 continued through 261 — Two definitions of power and a separate Asfar annotation: The entire lengthy note contrasts the theologians’ possibility of acting/not acting with the philosophers’ conditional definition. It questions each when understood through an added psychic will and then quotes, with abridgment, Tabatabai’s separate Asfar 6:307–308 annotation on the unconditioned efficient agent. The quote’s conclusion identifies both definitions with the agent’s freedom from necessitation imposed by act or non-act. It is not inserted into the Nihaya authorial body.

1428 vol. 2 261 nn. 1–4 — Definition sources, philosophical referent and Avicenna attribution: References for the conditional definition and knowledge of the best order, identification of the philosophers, and the attribution to Avicenna of conceptual as well as extensional identity were read. The editor’s bibliographic references have not been independently verified.

1428 vol. 2 261 n. 5 continued through 262 — Concept versus instance: The full argument distinguishes identity of instances, shared by all divine perfections, from identity of concepts. The editor argues that saying God knows and saying God wills do not convey the same concept. This reinforces the author’s objection but remains separately attributed exposition.

1428 vol. 2 262 nn. 1–4 — Orthographic emendations and references: Both explicit changes of مشيّة to مشيئة and the references to XII.10 and the end of this chapter were read. The normalized spelling is recorded as later editorial work; it is not treated as an early or manuscript reading.

1428 vol. 2 263 nn. 1–6 — References and grammatical changes: The backwards reference, philosopher/source citations, reference to the earlier editorial argument, gloss of ما بالها, addition of أن before تنتزع, and the change أن يتّصف به to أن تتّصف بها were all read. The earlier construction without أن is retained. The agreement change is disclosed as a later emendation, with the English’s plural interpretation made explicit.

1428 vol. 2 264 nn. 1–2 — Lexical preference and cross-reference: The later editor explicitly replaces العروض with العرض and refers to XII.10. The earlier العروض, conveying inherence or occurrence as an accident, is retained, consistently with the other retained loci.

Complete external comparison reconciled in Stage X. The early 1404 witness is a printed facsimile and the later 1428 witness is an edited digital presentation. No manuscript collation or independent human certification is claimed.

Adopted: ولم ينضمّ إليها إلاّ هيئآت عَرَضيّة → ولم ينضمّ إليهما إلاّ هيئآت عَرَضيّة. Adopt the explicit later dual pronoun referring to الطين والحجر. The early/base feminine singular has no suitable immediate feminine antecedent; English already says the added configurations without specifying the pronoun. Grade: explicit-later-editor-emendation. Source: 1404 pp. 106; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 180 n. 6

Adopted: such as swords, houses, and other artificial things. → as with artificial objects such as swords and houses, and with other composites of this kind.. The source ends كالسيف والبيت من الأمور الصناعية وغيرها. The existing English restricts the final others to artificial objects, whereas the source also allows other consideration-based compounds. Preserve that wider scope. Grade: English-scope-correction-against-both-external-witnesses. Source: 1404 pp. 106,107; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 180

Adopted: هيئآت → هيئات. Correct spelling of the plural configurations; both witnesses print هيئات. Two occurrences in the objection. Grade: jointly-attested-spelling-repair. Source: 1404 pp. 106; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 180

Adopted: المركّبات الإعتباريّه → المركّبات الإعتباريّة. Restore tāʾ marbūṭa; both witnesses print اعتبارية. Grade: jointly-attested-spelling-repair. Source: 1404 pp. 106; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 180

Adopted: آثاراً مختّصةً → آثاراً مختصّةً. Move the misplaced shadda from tāʾ to ṣād in مختصّة; not a new substantive variant. Grade: editorial-lexical-vocalization. Source: 1404 pp. 108; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 182

Adopted: وتلبُس الجسم → وتلبُّس الجسم. Restore the verbal noun تلبّس, qualification by the concepts; the source consonants are unchanged. Grade: contextual-vocalization; no-decisive-case-vowel-attestation-claimed. Source: 1404 pp. 106; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 179

Adopted: بالموضوع المشخِّصَ والأعراضَ الفعليّة → بالموضوع المشخَّصِ. والأعراضُ الفعليّة. Retain the early/base consonants المشخص but vocalize them passively: the subject is individuated, not an individuator. The adjective is genitive after بالموضوع; الأعراض begins the following nominal clause and is nominative. The punctuation separates the clauses. Later المتشخص expresses the same sense but adds a consonant and is not imported. Grade: contextual-vocalization-and-punctuation; early-consonants-preserved. Source: 1404 pp. 108; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 182

Adopted: الفصل السابع — في إثبات الصور النوعيّة وهي الصور الجوهريّة — المنوِّعة لجوهر الجسم المطلق → الفصل السابع — في إثبات الصور النوعيّة وهي الصور الجوهريّة المنوِّعة لجوهر الجسم المطلق. Remove the reader’s spurious em dash between noun and adjective; retain every original heading clause. Grade: editorial-punctuation; source-heading-clauses-preserved. Source: 1404 pp. 106; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 179

Adopted: Discrete quantity, namely number, necessarily exists externally. → Discrete quantity, namely number, self-evidently exists externally.. بالضرورة marks the asserted evident status of this existence claim. “Necessarily exists” can wrongly suggest the intrinsic necessary existence of an accidental quantity. Preserve the source’s epistemic claim without turning it into ontological necessity. Grade: English-modal-disambiguation-from-context; not-an-Arabic-variant. Source: 1404 pp. 110; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 187

Adopted: because there is a common measure among its instances. → because there is a common measure among their instances.. Preserve the early/base feminine أفرادها, whose nearest grammatical antecedent is the several kinds of motions. The current English singular its tacitly follows the later masculine أفراده referring to time. Their keeps the early reference to instances of those motions; disclose the later alternative separately. Grade: English-anaphoric-alignment-with-retained-early-reading. Source: 1404 pp. 110,111; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 188

Adopted: متناهيّةً → متناهيةً. Remove the spurious shadda on yāʾ in finite; consonants unchanged. Grade: editorial-lexical-vocalization. Source: 1404 pp. 110; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 188

Adopted: والمكّعب → والمكعّب. Move shadda from kāf to ʿayn in cube; both editions name the cube at this locus. Grade: editorial-lexical-vocalization. Source: 1404 pp. 111; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 188

Adopted: ثلاثةً أجزاء → ثلاثةِ أجزاء. The numeral is genitive after إلى and in construct with أجزاء, so it is neither accusative nor nunated. No decisive external case vowel is claimed. Grade: contextual-editorial-case-vocalization. Source: 1404 pp. 110; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 186

Adopted: قوّةً للجزء التالي → قوّةٌ للجزء التالي. قوة is the nominative predicate of إنّ كلّ جزء, not an accusative object; external consonants are unchanged. Grade: contextual-editorial-case-vocalization. Source: 1404 pp. 110; 1428 vol. 1 pp. 187
